description:
Wibou's idle: the clip he plays whenever he stands in a fight, between moves, while waiting and after landing.

Who he is. Wibou is an ironic mall-ninja weeaboo: a cringe Neo from The Matrix with a katana, a black fedora, a dark open coat, black trousers and white sneakers (images 1-2, the real character in the game). He takes himself completely seriously, which is the joke, so play every pose sincerely, never winking. In the fight he is a quick, light spacing duelist who wins at the edge of his blade's reach and then chases opponents into the air. He holds the katana in his right hand; its home on the ground is low by his right hip, the blade pointing out to his right and back, nearly level, the tip about 1.5 m out to the right and 1 m behind the hips.

How the game plays it. The idle loops: ticks 0-360 are 6 s, wrapping from 360 back to 0. Every ground move and the run start from it with a 0.05 s crossfade, and every landing settles into it over 0.1-0.15 s, so his feet, his stance and above all the sword's home must stay where today's idle has them (reference 'idle', tick 0). The match camera sits behind and above him.

Keep it calm. An idle is a bit of life while the player presses nothing, not a performance. Measured on today's hand-made idle: body joints turn 8.7 degrees per second on average and the hands move 0.08 body lengths a second against the hips. Stay at or below that outside the one gesture.

The pose: too cool. Feet planted where the idle has them, both soles flat. His weight sits on the back leg, the front knee soft. The chest is a touch back, chin up, the head tilted a few degrees: the composure of a hero in a film he has watched too many times. The left hand hangs loose by his side. The sword hand is low by the right hip with the blade out to the right and back, nearly level, as in the idle.

The loop:
- One slow breath per loop: inhale over about ticks 0-150, the chest rising 1.5-4 cm and the shoulders lifting a little, then a long exhale. The hips drift 1-3 cm with the weight, never more.
- The blade tip sinks and lifts a few centimetres 3-4 ticks after the chest, as the wrist lets it hang.
- One slow gesture, ticks about 180-260: the left hand rises, thumb and forefinger find the front of the hat brim and tip it down a few degrees, and the hand drifts back to his side. The head dips into the touch and comes back a few ticks after the hand leaves. Slow and sure, never a flick.
- Offset everything so nothing peaks on the same tick: chest first, shoulders and head later, the blade last.
- The feet stay planted the whole time. No steps, no spins, no attack.

Secondary motion, with numbers (all inside the calm budget):
- Coat: the hips drift 1-3 cm and turn 1-3 degrees with the weight over the loop; that is what swings the coat springs.
- Hat: the fedora rides the head, so the head trails the chest by 4-8 ticks and nods or tilts 1-3 degrees with the breath. In the gesture the brim dips 4-8 degrees and the head comes back 6-10 ticks after the hand leaves it.
- Sword: the wrist lets the blade hang. The tip sinks and lifts 3-8 cm, 3-6 ticks after the chest, and after the gesture it settles with one small overshoot (under 1 cm), never a wobble.

Overlap and follow-through everywhere: the hips lead, the chest trails 1-3 ticks, the head and arms trail more, and the sword hand trails its forearm 2-4 ticks so the blade settles after the body (Clip.overlap()). Holds are moving holds, never a repeated pose. Cartoony and readable, not mocap. The coat chains are in the pack, but a spring drives them in the game: leave them at rest, and give the hips and spine real motion for the springs to follow. Keep each hand in line with its forearm (wrists under 45 degrees). The blade never passes through the head, the hat, the body or the legs, and it is never pointed straight at the match camera behind him: it always keeps a clear sideways part so its length reads.
